newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Tel Aviv exchange asks to delay new trading system.
newsitem.headline: Tel Aviv exchange asks to delay new trading system.

text.p: The Tel Aviv Stock Exchange (TASE) said on Monday it would recommend to its board delaying the introduction of computerised continuous trading to August 14 from July 20.

"Postponement of the date for launching the system will enable members of the exchange and the exchange itself to check the system over a period of several weeks under conditions identical to those in actual trading," the TASE.
The TASE said the directors would consider the delay at its meeting July 10.
Introduction of continuous trading has been delayed before, but TASE officials have denied they are experiencing technical problems.
The new system will initially be used to trade about 10 stocks from the Mishtanim list of top 100 shares and after a month of trials expanded to the blue chip shares of the Maof 25 index.

The TASE now uses a system it calls "semi-continuous trading" for its heavy capitalisation shares. The new system is aimed at making the TASE more closely resemble trading systems elsewhere in the world.
